transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I came in because I just can’t stop focusing on this sagging, uneven area around my jaw and neck. People tell me it looks normal, but I feel like it’s the first thing people notice—families, nurses, people at church—when they look at me.
Is it just your appearance that's bothering you, or are there other things that you're concerned about as well?

It’s mostly my appearance, honestly. I keep getting stuck on this sagging, uneven part around my jaw and neck. Even when people tell me it looks normal, I still feel like it’s what families, nurses, or people at church notice first when they look at me.
Is this concern about your jaw and neck area affecting your daily life or activities in any way?

Yes, it is. I’ve passed up chances at work to help lead meetings or take on more supervisory tasks because I’m afraid everyone will be looking at my face and neck. And sometimes I fall behind on paperwork because I get stuck trying to make myself look presentable first.

I’ve also stopped going to some of my book club and walking club things. Getting ready just feels like too much, and then I end up not going.
Does your concern about the sagging, uneven area around your jaw and neck stay the same all the time, or are there moments when it bothers you less?

It does bother me most of the time. I mean, there might be little moments when I’m busy and not thinking about it as much, but it doesn’t really go away. I keep noticing that sagging, uneven spot around my jaw and neck, and even if people say it looks normal, I still feel like it’s the first thing they see when they look at me.
Do you think your jaw and neck area actually looks uneven and sagging, or is it just that you feel like it appears that way to others?

I think it really does look uneven and sagging. I know people tell me it looks normal, but I can’t stop seeing that spot around my jaw and neck. It feels like it’s the first thing families, nurses, or people at church notice when they look at me.
Do you think there's any possibility that your jaw and neck area might actually look normal to other people, even if it doesn't look that way to you?

I guess there’s a possibility, because people do tell me it looks normal. But when I look at myself, I just can’t see it that way. I keep seeing that sagging, uneven spot around my jaw and neck, and it feels like it’s the first thing people notice—families, nurses, people at church, everybody.
Do you think that your view of your jaw and neck area is possibly not accurate?

Maybe… I mean, I know people keep telling me it looks normal, so I guess it’s possible I’m not seeing it right. But to me, I can’t stop noticing that sagging, uneven spot around my jaw and neck. It feels like that’s what families, nurses, or people at church see first when they look at me.
Have you ever had a time when you didn't think your jaw and neck area looked uneven and sagging?

Not really, not lately. I mean, I came in because I can’t stop seeing that sagging, uneven spot around my jaw and neck. Even when people tell me it looks normal, I still feel like it’s the first thing people notice when they look at me.
Do you find yourself repeating certain behaviors, like checking your appearance in the mirror, over and over again?

Yes. Before I leave for work or if I have a meeting, I’ll keep going back to the bathroom mirror and checking it. I fix my collar or my hair around my neck, then I’ll look again in my phone camera. Sometimes I ask my daughter if it looks strange. It’s gotten me late more than once.
Do you feel like you have to check your appearance in the mirror, or can you stop if you want to?

It feels like I have to check. I can try to stop, but then I get this nagging feeling that it looks wrong, so I go back to the bathroom mirror again. Before work or a meeting I’ll fix my collar or my hair around my neck, then check my phone camera too. Sometimes I ask my daughter if it looks strange. It’s made me late more than once.
How would you describe the level of distress you feel when you think about the sagging, uneven area around your jaw and neck?

It’s pretty upsetting. I came in because I just can’t stop seeing that sagging, uneven part around my jaw and neck. Even when people say it looks normal, I still feel like it’s the first thing families, nurses, or people at church notice when they look at me.
Is your concern about your appearance the only thing that's been bothering you, or have you been having other worries or fears lately?
I’m not really sure. The main thing I’ve been focused on is my neck and jaw area. I can’t think of another big fear or worry lately that feels separate from that.
Do you feel like checking your appearance is something you can control?

Not really. I mean, I can tell myself I’m done, but before I leave for work or a meeting I keep going back to the bathroom mirror. I’ll fix my collar and my hair around my neck, then check my phone camera again. Sometimes I’ll even ask my daughter if it looks strange. It’s hard to stop once I start, and it’s made me late more than once.
Have you avoided or had difficulty with any social interactions because of your concerns about your appearance?

Yes. I’ve turned down chances to help lead meetings or take on more supervisory parts at work because I feel like people will be staring at my face and neck. And sometimes I get stuck trying to make myself look okay before I leave, so I fall behind on paperwork.

Outside of work, I’ve skipped some book club and walking club things too. Getting ready just feels like too much, and I end up not going.
Do you think that other people actually notice the sagging, uneven area around your jaw and neck, or is it just that you feel self-conscious about it?

I think they notice it. I know people tell me it looks normal, but I just can’t stop seeing that sagging, uneven spot around my jaw and neck. It feels like when families, nurses, or people at church look at me, that’s the first thing they see.
Do you think your view of your jaw and neck area could change over time, or do you feel like it's something that will always look this way to you?

I want to think it could change, but honestly it feels like it always looks that way to me. I came in because I can’t stop seeing that sagging, uneven spot around my jaw and neck. Even when people tell me it looks normal, I still feel like it’s the first thing families, nurses, or people at church notice when they look at me.
Has your concern about your jaw and neck area affected your relationships with family or friends?

Yes, it has. I don’t go to some things with friends like I used to, like book club or walking club, because getting ready feels like too much and I get embarrassed about my face and neck.

And at work, I’ve passed up chances to help lead meetings or take on more responsibility because I worry people will be looking at me. So I guess it has made me pull back from people some.
Has your concern about your jaw and neck area caused you to avoid any important life events or activities that you would have otherwise participated in?

Yes. I’ve stopped going to some of my book club and walking club things because just getting ready feels like too much, and I get too embarrassed.

At work, too, I’ve passed up chances to help lead meetings or do more supervisory-type things because I worry everyone will be looking at my face and neck. And sometimes I fall behind on paperwork because I get stuck trying to make myself look presentable before I can move on.
Do you ever find yourself thinking about the sagging, uneven area around your jaw and neck when you're trying to focus on something else?

Yes. It pops into my head even when I’m trying to do something else. I’ll be focused on work or talking to someone, and then I start thinking they must be noticing that sagging, uneven part around my jaw and neck. Even when people say it looks normal, I can’t seem to stop seeing it.
